name: nlp_serving
title: The serving side of an NLP project: a BPE tokenizer trainer, a BLEU/ROUGE scoring script and a batching inference service
origin: hardening round 1, domain-nlp, 2026-09-13 - three correct programs that look like training code and must produce nothing
note: Measured 0 findings in both --dataflow local and --dataflow ip on 2026-09-13. One config_warning is emitted and is correct: the relevance prefilter sets tokenizer_train.py aside because `tokenizers` is in no knowledge table, so 2 of 3 files are analyzed. That file's forbidden rows below therefore assert what must not fire once it is analyzed - run with --relevance all to check them.

forbidden.why: IntentService.__init__ calls self.model.eval() on line 36, before any request can reach predict()
predict() carries the @torch.no_grad() decorator (line 57), which is one of the two forms MLV302's detection reads
input_ids and attention_mask are both moved to self.device on lines 61-62, and the model was moved to the same device on line 35
the device is the literal 'cpu' by default and is a constructor argument, not a hard-coded cuda string

there is no training loop, no split and no model fit anywhere in this project - a service that only serves has nothing to seed, and MLV601's own detection requires a train loop or a SPLIT/fit call to exist
there is no DataLoader in this project; batching is the service's own queue
probabilities.max(dim=-1) returns the argmax index, which is what the label lookup uses - no class metric is computed here at all
the softmax on line 65 feeds a label lookup, not a cross-entropy loss; no loss exists in this project
IntentService is a plain class, not an nn.Module subclass, so the super().__init__() requirement does not apply to it
self.pending is a list of Request dataclasses, not of modules
nothing is saved or loaded with torch in this project; the model comes from from_pretrained
scoring saved generations involves no randomness at all
BLEU and ROUGE take strings; no class metric is computed
training a BPE vocabulary is deterministic given the corpus and the vocab size; there is no split and no model here despite the file being full of the word `train`
tokenizer.train(files, trainer) is a vocabulary fit, not a gradient loop - there is no optimizer in this project
the tokenizer is fitted on the whole corpus on purpose: a subword vocabulary is part of the model's input contract, not a statistic learned from labels, and no split exists in this project

unsupported.defect: nothing in this project validates the model it serves - which is correct here, because the evaluation lives in evaluate_predictions.py, and is the shape MLV304 would have to tell apart from a project with no evaluation at all
unsupported.why: MLV304 (no validation loop at all) is a later-tier rule and is not built; it is recorded here because this file is the trap it will have to survive

unsupported.defect: nothing checks that MAX_LENGTH here equals the MAX_LENGTH the training script tokenised with; a mismatch silently truncates differently at serve time
unsupported.why: MLV901 (preprocessing applied in training but missing on the inference path) is a later-tier rule and is not built, and it would need the two projects analyzed together

unsupported.defect: the tokenizer and the model are loaded from the same checkpoint directory here, which is correct, but nothing would notice if they were not
unsupported.why: MLV902 (tokenizer/checkpoint identifier mismatch) is a later-tier rule and is not built
